Finding: Shell structures BagMRU, Bags, and MuiCache were present.
Interpretation: The acquired UsrClass snapshot contains Windows shell-state artifacts suitable for user-activity correlation.

Finding: BagMRU contained 62 immediate subkeys and 65 values, including NodeSlots, NodeSlot, MRUListEx, and numbered entries 0 through 61.
Interpretation: A substantial ShellBag structure is present. Presence alone does not identify the human responsible for the recorded shell activity.

Finding: Root MRUListEx contained all 62 numbered entries followed by a -1 terminator.
Interpretation: The value provides relative ordering of root BagMRU entries but does not independently provide exact interaction timestamps.

Finding: Readable fragments included C:\, Users, Ifean, AppData, GitHub, Desktop/DESKTO~1, Documents/DOCUME~1, Pictures, and CAMERA~1.
Interpretation: These strings were recovered from binary Shell Item data and are treated as investigative leads rather than fully parsed paths.

Finding: Best-effort extraction recovered references to D:\, E:\, F:\, and G:\ within BagMRU binary data.
Interpretation: These drive-letter references support the presence of shell-state data associated with multiple volumes. They do not independently identify the underlying physical device or establish file transfer.

Finding: Recursive reg.exe text search returned 0 matches for SanDisk.
Interpretation: No readable SanDisk string was identified by this search method. This is a scoped negative and does not establish that the device was never represented by ShellBag data.

Finding: Recursive reg.exe text search returned 0 matches for Board-Financial-Plan-2027.xlsx.
Interpretation: No readable match for the training-case filename was identified by this search method. This does not establish that the file never existed or was never accessed.

Finding: Shell Item binary structures were examined using best-effort ASCII/UTF-16 string extraction rather than a dedicated ShellBag parser.
Interpretation: Recovered fragments were not used to reconstruct complete paths or make unsupported claims about exact folder traversal, physical-user attribution, or file copying.
